```python
# filename: segment_and_find_oldest_bluray.py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

file_path = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/32102e3e-d12a-4209-9163-7b3a104efe5d.xlsx'

df = pd.read_excel(file_path, skiprows=2)
format_headers = {'DVD','Blu-Ray'}

# Create Format column by propagating the last seen format header in Title
fmt = []
current = None
for t in df['Title'].fillna(''):
    tt = str(t).strip()
    if tt in format_headers:
        current = tt
        fmt.append(current)
    else:
        fmt.append(current)

df['Format'] = fmt

# Filter Blu-Ray entries (exclude the header row itself)
bluray_df = df[(df['Format']=='Blu-Ray') & (~df['Title'].isin(format_headers))].copy()
# Convert Year to numeric and drop NaNs
bluray_df['Year'] = pd.to_numeric(bluray_df['Year'], errors='coerce')
bluray_df = bluray_df.dropna(subset=['Year'])
# Find oldest and print title
oldest_year = bluray_df['Year'].min()
oldest_title = bluray_df.loc[bluray_df['Year']==oldest_year, 'Title'].iloc[0]
print(oldest_title)
```
